item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship 2027, an international, fully remote opportunity designed for early-career researchers working in the field of children’s learning and development.

The six-month program provides selected researchers with professional training, expert mentorship, practical science communication experience, opportunities to publish their work for a global audience, and a CHF 5,000 stipend to support the time and resources required to participate in the Fellowship.

Launched by BOLD as the platform celebrates a decade of communicating scientific knowledge about child learning and development, the Fellowship seeks researchers who want to take their scientific expertise beyond traditional academic audiences and make evidence-based knowledge accessible to caregivers, educators, and other people who directly support children.

The Fellowship is fully remote and part-time, meaning participants can take part from anywhere in the world while continuing their existing research or professional responsibilities. Up to three researchers will be selected for the inaugural Fellowship cohort.

Applications opened on 1 September 2026 and will close on 31 October 2026.

About BOLD

BOLD is a global platform dedicated to sharing scientific knowledge that can improve children’s learning and development.

The platform connects researchers, journalists, practitioners, educators, and other specialists interested in understanding how children learn, develop, and thrive.

Rather than limiting important scientific findings to academic journals or specialist conferences, BOLD aims to make rigorous research understandable and useful to wider audiences.

Its content focuses on evidence-based information that caregivers and educators can use to make informed decisions when supporting children and young people.

BOLD covers areas connected with:

  • Child and youth development
  • Learning and education
  • Psychology
  • Neuroscience
  • Genetics
  • Mental and physical health
  • Learning environments
  • Education systems
  • Technology and learning
  • Parenting and childcare
  • Teaching methods
  • Equity and inclusion
  • Society and child development

BOLD describes itself as a global scientific knowledge platform that empowers caregivers and educators with information and tools that can help children learn and develop. Its wider network includes researchers, journalists, and practitioners committed to communicating current scientific thinking in accessible ways.

About the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship was created to help researchers become more effective communicators of scientific knowledge.

Researchers often produce valuable evidence that could influence education, parenting, child development, and public understanding. However, academic research can be difficult for non-specialist audiences to understand because findings are commonly communicated through technical papers, specialist terminology, statistical language, and academic conferences.

The BOLD Fellowship aims to help bridge this gap.

Selected Fellows will learn how to translate complex scientific ideas into accessible and engaging information for audiences outside academia.

This includes communicating with people such as:

  • Parents and caregivers
  • Teachers
  • Education professionals
  • Practitioners
  • Members of the public
  • Other audiences interested in child learning and development

During the six-month program, Fellows will receive dedicated mentoring and training while simultaneously putting those skills into practice by creating content for BOLD’s audience.

Rather than functioning only as a classroom-style training course, the Fellowship combines professional development with real publishing experience. Fellows will develop articles, interviews, videos, or other agreed content that can ultimately appear on BOLD’s website and social media platforms.

BOLD Science Communication Fellowship Stipend

One of the major features of the program is its financial support.

Each selected Fellow will receive a CHF 5,000 stipend.

According to BOLD, the stipend is intended to cover the time and resources participants invest in fulfilling the requirements of the Fellowship.

Payment will be made in two stages:

  • 50% of the stipend will be awarded when the Fellowship begins.
  • 50% will be awarded at the end of the Fellowship after the Fellow successfully completes the required activities, tasks, and milestones.

This means the total available financial support for each Fellow is CHF 5,000.

Applicants should understand that this funding is connected to participation and completion of the Fellowship requirements rather than being described as an unrestricted research grant.

Fully Remote and Part-Time Program

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship has been structured to make participation possible for researchers based around the world.

The program is:

Fully remote: Participants do not need to relocate to another country or travel to a physical BOLD office to complete the Fellowship.

Part-time: The Fellowship has been designed to fit alongside a participant’s existing research or professional role.

BOLD expects Fellows to dedicate approximately six hours per month to content development and participation in virtual training sessions.

This relatively flexible structure means selected researchers can continue their existing academic or professional commitments while participating in the program.

Fellowship Duration

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship will run for approximately six months.

The official program dates are:

Fellowship begins: 4 January 2027

Fellowship ends: 30 June 2027

Fellows will also be expected to participate in a virtual introduction during January 2027.

How Many Fellows Will Be Selected?

The program is highly focused and will select up to three researchers.

These researchers will participate in the six-month Fellowship while receiving individualized training, mentorship, and opportunities to develop public-facing content.

Because only a small number of researchers will be selected, prospective applicants should prepare their application materials carefully and demonstrate both their scientific expertise and their interest in communicating research to audiences beyond academia.

What Selected BOLD Fellows Will Receive

Successful applicants will gain access to several professional-development opportunities covering writing, editing, public communication, and multimedia science communication.

1. Writing Workshop with BOLD’s Editor-in-Chief

Fellows will participate in a writing workshop led by BOLD’s Editor-in-Chief.

The workshop is expected to help researchers improve their ability to translate scientific concepts into clear and compelling language for general audiences.

Academic writing and public science communication require different approaches. A research paper may prioritize methodology, precision, technical terminology, and citations, while public communication must often explain the same concepts clearly without overwhelming readers with specialist language.

The workshop will therefore provide practical experience in adapting scientific knowledge for non-academic audiences.

2. Editing Training

Fellows will receive training in editing both:

  • Their own work
  • The work of their colleagues

Learning to edit effectively is an important science communication skill because good communication involves more than generating an initial draft.

Researchers must learn how to identify unnecessary complexity, clarify arguments, improve structure, strengthen explanations, and ensure scientific accuracy while making material understandable to non-specialists.

The peer-editing element can also help Fellows develop skills in giving constructive editorial feedback.

3. Monthly Writing Club

Selected Fellows will participate in a monthly writing club with the BOLD team.

This provides a regular structure for practicing science communication, receiving input, developing ideas, and remaining engaged with the Fellowship community throughout the six-month program.

4. Training in Science Communication Videos

Modern science communication increasingly takes place through digital and social media.

The Fellowship therefore includes expert training on producing science communication videos for social media.

This aspect of the program can help researchers learn how to explain complex topics in formats suitable for platforms where audiences often consume information quickly and visually.

Participants can consequently develop communication capabilities extending beyond traditional academic writing.

5. Training in Writing for General Audiences

Fellows will also receive expert instruction in writing scientific information for general audiences.

This training is particularly important because the primary audience for BOLD includes caregivers and educators rather than only scientists.

Participants will need to communicate evidence accurately without assuming that readers have specialist knowledge of statistics, psychology, neuroscience, education research, or other technical fields.

What Fellows Are Expected to Do

Participation in the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship comes with specific responsibilities.

Selected researchers will be expected to:

  1. Attend a virtual introduction in January 2027.
  2. Dedicate approximately six hours per month to content development and participation in virtual training activities.
  3. Produce at least three pieces of content during the Fellowship.

Depending on discussions with BOLD’s Editor-in-Chief, these outputs may include:

  • Articles
  • Interviews
  • Videos

The final pieces will be published through BOLD’s website and social media channels.

This publication component is particularly valuable because Fellows are not simply practicing communication exercises privately. They have the opportunity to produce work intended for real audiences.

Who Can Apply for the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship?

The Fellowship is intended for scientists researching children’s learning and development.

According to the official eligibility criteria, applicants must:

  • Be a scientist studying an aspect of children’s learning and development
  • Be an active researcher
  • Be no more than 10 years post-PhD

However, an important aspect of the eligibility rules is that applicants do not need to hold a PhD to apply.

This means the program is aimed broadly at early-career researchers rather than being exclusively restricted to people who already hold a doctoral qualification.

Do You Need a PhD to Apply?

No.

BOLD explicitly states that applicants do not need a PhD to apply.

The reference to being no more than 10 years post-PhD establishes an upper career-stage limit for researchers who have completed a doctorate, but it does not make a doctorate mandatory.

Applicants must nevertheless be active researchers working on areas related to children’s learning and development.

Relevant Research Fields

BOLD does not restrict eligibility to one narrowly defined academic discipline.

Researchers may potentially work across fields connected to children’s learning and development, provided their research is relevant to the Fellowship’s focus.

Potential areas may include, depending on the applicant’s research topic:

  • Developmental psychology
  • Education
  • Educational psychology
  • Neuroscience
  • Cognitive science
  • Child development
  • Learning sciences
  • Language development
  • Mental health
  • Child and adolescent development
  • Education technology
  • Social development
  • Behavioral science
  • Genetics and development
  • Teaching and learning
  • Public health topics connected to child development

The key requirement is that the applicant is a scientist studying an aspect of children’s learning and development. Applicants should therefore explain clearly how their research connects with BOLD’s mission and audience.

Applicants from All Countries Can Apply

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship is a global opportunity.

BOLD specifically states that applicants are welcome from anywhere in the world.

Because the Fellowship is conducted remotely, successful candidates can participate without relocating internationally.

There is no country-specific restriction stated on the official Fellowship page.

This gives eligible researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania, and other regions an opportunity to compete for the Fellowship, provided they satisfy the research and career-stage criteria.

Application Requirements

Applications must be submitted in English through BOLD’s official application form.

Applicants need to prepare three principal components.

1. Science Communication Sample

Applicants must provide either a sample article or video explaining a scientific concept relevant to BOLD in a way that is accessible to caregivers.

The recommended maximum length is:

  • Approximately 500 words for an article, or
  • Approximately three minutes for a video

Applicants who have already written or presented something for a public audience can provide a link to that work.

Those who do not already have a suitable public-facing science communication example can instead upload a written piece.

2. Written Statement

Applicants must submit a written statement of up to 500 words.

The statement should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to participate in the Fellowship
  • Why the applicant believes they would be a good fit for the program

This is an important opportunity to demonstrate motivation, communication ability, alignment with BOLD’s mission, and a genuine interest in translating research for caregivers and educators.

3. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must also submit their CV.

The CV should include any previous science communication experience.

Researchers who have communicated science through public articles, talks, videos, podcasts, workshops, social media, outreach events, teaching, or related activities may therefore want to ensure that relevant experience is clearly presented.

Application Language

All required application materials must be submitted in English.

This includes the science communication sample, written statement, and associated application materials submitted through the official form.

Who Will Review the Applications?

Applications will be reviewed by:

Annie Brookman-Byrne, Editor-in-Chief of BOLD

and

Gemma Wirz, Learning Outreach Lead at the Jacobs Foundation.

The involvement of both editorial and learning-outreach leadership reflects the Fellowship’s emphasis on combining scientific quality with effective communication for public audiences.

BOLD Science Communication Fellowship 2027 Timeline

Applicants should take note of the following official dates:

1 September 2026: Applications open

31 October 2026: Applications close

November 2026: Applications reviewed

1 December 2026: Selected Fellows informed

4 January 2027: Fellowship begins

30 June 2027: Fellowship ends

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship is:

31 October 2026

Applicants should prepare and submit their materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Because a science communication sample and a tailored statement are required, candidates should allow sufficient time to prepare strong materials that demonstrate their ability to explain scientific concepts clearly.

How to Apply for the BOLD Science Communication Fellowship

Applications are submitted online through the official application form linked from BOLD’s Fellowship page.

Before beginning the application, candidates should prepare:

  1. A science communication article of ideally no more than 500 words or a video of ideally no more than three minutes
  2. A written statement of up to 500 words explaining their motivation and suitability
  3. A current CV including relevant science communication experience

Applicants should ensure that all application materials are prepared in English.

The official Fellowship page provides access to the application form and should be used as the primary source for application instructions and any future updates.

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Early-Career Researchers

Scientific expertise alone does not guarantee that research will influence practice.

For evidence to benefit families, educators, policymakers, or communities, research findings need to be communicated in a way that non-specialists can understand and use.

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship addresses this challenge by giving scientists practical experience in translating their research expertise into accessible public communication.

The combination of mentoring, writing instruction, editing practice, video training, publishing opportunities, and financial support makes the Fellowship particularly relevant for researchers who want to develop a stronger public-facing profile.

For an early-career scientist, these skills may be useful across multiple professional pathways, including:

  • Academic research
  • Public engagement
  • Science journalism
  • Education
  • Research communications
  • Policy engagement
  • Knowledge translation
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Public-facing science platforms
  • Research outreach

Opportunity to Build a Published Science Communication Portfolio

Another significant feature of the Fellowship is that participants will create at least three pieces of content for BOLD.

Depending on the format agreed with the Editor-in-Chief, these may include articles, interviews, or videos.

Having published examples of science communication can help researchers demonstrate that they are able to translate technical knowledge for wider audiences.

For researchers interested in science communication, public engagement, journalism, policy translation, or outreach roles, this type of portfolio can be professionally valuable.

Commitment Required from Fellows

The program is intended to complement, rather than replace, a researcher’s existing professional role.

Fellows should expect to commit approximately six hours each month to training and content-development activities.

However, applicants should not interpret the relatively modest monthly time requirement as meaning that participation requires little effort.

Successful Fellows will be expected to:

  • Engage seriously with training
  • Participate in the program’s virtual activities
  • Develop publishable content
  • Respond to editorial feedback
  • Complete agreed milestones
  • Produce at least three final pieces of content

Completion of required tasks and milestones is also relevant to receiving the second half of the CHF 5,000 stipend.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants should pay particular attention to the science communication sample because it provides direct evidence of their ability to explain research to a non-specialist audience.

A strong submission should generally aim to:

  • Explain one clear scientific idea
  • Minimize unnecessary technical terminology
  • Define technical concepts that cannot be avoided
  • Make the topic relevant to caregivers or educators
  • Maintain scientific accuracy
  • Use clear and engaging language
  • Demonstrate an understanding of BOLD’s audience

The motivation statement should complement the communication sample rather than simply repeating the applicant’s CV.

Applicants should explain why science communication matters to them, what they hope to learn from the Fellowship, how their research relates to children’s learning and development, and how they intend to use the communication skills gained through the program.

Key Details at a Glance

Program: BOLD Science Communication Fellowship

Cohort: 2027

Host: BOLD

Supported by: Jacobs Foundation

Program format: Fully remote

Participation: Part-time

Number of Fellows: Up to three researchers

Stipend: CHF 5,000

Payment arrangement: 50% at the beginning and 50% after successful completion of required Fellowship tasks and milestones

Approximate commitment: Six hours per month

Program start: 4 January 2027

Program end: 30 June 2027

Application opens: 1 September 2026

Application deadline: 31 October 2026

Application language: English

Geographic eligibility: Worldwide

PhD required: No

Main target group: Active researchers studying children’s learning and development

Career-stage limit: No more than 10 years post-PhD for applicants who hold a PhD

Required outputs: At least three articles, interviews, or videos agreed with the Editor-in-Chief and published through BOLD’s website and social media channels.

Conclusion

The BOLD Science Communication Fellowship 2027 offers an excellent opportunity for early-career researchers studying children’s learning and development to build practical skills in communicating science beyond academia.

With a CHF 5,000 stipend, expert training in writing and editing, guidance on science communication videos, a monthly writing club, professional mentoring, and opportunities to publish content for BOLD’s international audience, the program combines structured learning with hands-on communication experience.

Its fully remote and part-time format also makes the Fellowship accessible to eligible researchers around the world without requiring relocation or interruption of their existing research careers.

Applicants do not need to hold a PhD, although they must be active researchers studying an aspect of children’s learning and development and fall within the program’s early-career criteria.

Applications opened on 1 September 2026 and the final deadline is 31 October 2026. Successful Fellows will be informed on 1 December 2026, with the Fellowship beginning on 4 January 2027 and continuing until 30 June 2027.

Researchers who are passionate about making scientific evidence understandable and useful to caregivers, educators, and wider public audiences are encouraged to prepare their applications carefully and apply before the deadline.

For more global opportunities, click HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme 2026 is inviting young people living in Cyprus to apply for an opportunity to develop practical skills in environmental peacebuilding, intercommunal cooperation, youth leadership and sustainable development.

Organized by the United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus (UNFICYP) in partnership with the British Council, through its regional Youth Connect programme, the initiative will bring together young people from different communities across the island to learn, collaborate and develop joint environmental actions.

The programme is designed for young people who are interested in environmental protection, peacebuilding, climate action, social cohesion and community development. Participants will take part in immersive workshops, work in intercommunal teams, receive guidance from mentors and develop environmental initiatives that must be implemented by February 2027.

Participation in the programme is free. The application deadline is 20 September 2026.

Overview of the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme

The UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace initiative is being offered for the sixth year by UNFICYP and the British Council. The 2026 edition will focus specifically on environmental peacebuilding and the development of joint actions addressing shared environmental concerns.

Environmental challenges such as climate change, resource scarcity, pollution, environmental degradation and unequal access to resources can affect communities across social, political and geographical divisions. The programme recognizes that environmental issues can also provide opportunities for cooperation, dialogue and trust-building.

Through collaborative learning and practical action, the programme seeks to empower young people in Cyprus to become active contributors to a more peaceful, sustainable and inclusive future.

The initiative will enable participants to:

  • Explore the relationship between environmental challenges and peacebuilding.
  • Learn how shared environmental concerns can encourage cooperation.
  • Develop practical environmental action plans with participants from different communities.
  • Strengthen leadership, communication and teamwork skills.
  • Build relationships with environmental and peacebuilding practitioners.
  • Participate in initiatives that promote intercommunal trust and social cohesion.
  • Join a wider network of Youth Champions working on environmental and peace-related issues.

According to the official announcement, the programme is taking place at a time when climate change is increasingly contributing to insecurity, inequality and social vulnerability. The initiative therefore emphasizes the importance of acting both locally and collectively to address shared challenges.

What Is Environmental Peacebuilding?

Environmental peacebuilding refers to the use of environmental cooperation, natural-resource management and sustainability initiatives to support peace, prevent conflict and strengthen relationships between communities.

Environmental concerns often affect people regardless of their political, cultural, ethnic or social background. Issues such as water, waste management, biodiversity, climate resilience, land use, food systems and pollution can create shared interests and provide opportunities for constructive cooperation.

Within the UN Youth Champions programme, participants will explore how environmental action can contribute to:

  • Peaceful relationships between communities.
  • Mutual understanding and trust.
  • Sustainable development.
  • Inclusive youth leadership.
  • Climate resilience.
  • Community participation.
  • Environmental awareness.
  • Cooperation across the divide in Cyprus.

Rather than focusing only on discussions, the programme encourages participants to work together on practical initiatives that address environmental issues and benefit communities across the island.

Key Dates for the 2026 Programme

Applicants should take note of the important dates and participation requirements.

Programme Activity Date or Period
Application deadline 20 September 2026
Notification of successful applicants Expected by 23 September 2026
First workshop day 3 October 2026
Second workshop day 4 October 2026
Third workshop day 10 October 2026
Fourth workshop day 11 October 2026
Environmental action implementation deadline February 2027
Closing event End of March 2027

Attendance at all four workshop days is mandatory. Participants are also expected to actively contribute to the development and implementation of their team’s environmental action.

Who Can Apply for the UN Youth Champions Programme?

The programme is open to young people aged 18 to 30 who live in Cyprus and come from any community on the island.

Applicants do not need to have previous professional or academic experience in environmental protection, peacebuilding or activism. However, they should demonstrate genuine interest, motivation and willingness to work collaboratively with people from different communities.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Be between 18 and 30 years old.
  • Belong to or live within any community in Cyprus.
  • Have a strong desire to contribute to a peaceful and sustainable future on the island.
  • Demonstrate an interest in environmental issues and peacebuilding.
  • Be willing to become active in environmental and peace-related initiatives.
  • Commit to attending all four experiential workshop days on 3, 4, 10 and 11 October 2026.
  • Be willing to work with a team to develop and implement an environmental action by February 2027.
  • Have a very good knowledge of English.
  • Be willing to build interpersonal relationships with participants from all communities living in Cyprus.
  • Be interested in working collaboratively toward a common cause.
  • Not have previously benefited from a UN Youth Champions programme.

The call is intended to encourage participation from young people across the different communities in Cyprus. The organizers also seek gender diversity and equal representation among participants.

Previous Experience Is Not Required

One of the important features of the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme is that applicants do not need previous experience in environmental peacebuilding, environmental activism or related fields.

This makes the programme suitable for young people who may be new to environmental action but are passionate about sustainability, peace, youth participation, community development or social change.

Applicants do not necessarily need to be environmental scientists, peacebuilding professionals or climate activists. What matters is their:

  • Interest in the subject.
  • Willingness to learn.
  • Commitment to teamwork.
  • Ability to participate fully.
  • Motivation to contribute to a peaceful and sustainable Cyprus.

Participants will receive learning opportunities and support from experts, trainers, environmental practitioners, peacebuilding specialists and youth activists.

What Does the Programme Offer?

The UN Youth Champions initiative provides a combination of workshops, collaborative learning, mentoring, practical project development and networking opportunities.

1. Immersive Environmental Peacebuilding Workshops

The programme will include in-person workshops on:

  • 3 October 2026
  • 4 October 2026
  • 10 October 2026
  • 11 October 2026

The workshops will take place at Ledra Palace in the UN buffer zone in Nicosia.

The sessions will focus on experiential and collaborative learning. Participants will engage in interactive discussions, group activities, presentations and practical exercises related to environmental issues and peacebuilding.

The workshops are expected to help participants understand:

  • The links between environmental challenges and conflict.
  • The role of youth in peacebuilding.
  • The importance of environmental cooperation.
  • The value of inclusive leadership.
  • Ways to design community-focused environmental actions.
  • How to work effectively in intercommunal teams.

2. Team-Based Project Development

During the workshops, participants will meet other young people from communities across Cyprus. They will form teams and work together to identify environmental concerns that can be addressed through joint action.

Each team will develop an environmental action idea with support from programme organizers, experts and mentors.

The projects are expected to encourage cooperation across the divide and should be designed to reach people from different communities. Although actions may take place in specific locations, participants are strongly encouraged to develop initiatives that can benefit communities throughout Cyprus.

3. Mentorship and Expert Support

Each team will receive support from a mentor as it develops and implements its environmental action plan.

Mentors and experts may assist participants with:

  • Refining their project idea.
  • Identifying the environmental issue to address.
  • Developing an achievable action plan.
  • Preparing a simple project proposal.
  • Organizing implementation activities.
  • Identifying target beneficiaries.
  • Strengthening teamwork and communication.
  • Addressing practical challenges during implementation.

This guidance is intended to help participants transform an initial idea into a realistic and useful environmental initiative.

4. Small Grants for Environmental Actions

After the workshops, teams will be expected to finalize their environmental action ideas and submit a simple proposal.

Each team will receive a small grant to support the implementation of its approved environmental action. The supplied announcement does not specify the exact amount of funding available to each team.

The environmental actions must be implemented by February 2027.

The projects should:

  • Address a relevant environmental concern.
  • Encourage cooperation between communities.
  • Promote sustainability or environmental awareness.
  • Involve young people or local communities where appropriate.
  • Contribute to social cohesion and mutual understanding.
  • Be practical and achievable within the programme timeline.
  • Reach people across the divide.

The grant is intended to support the implementation of team projects. It should not be interpreted as a personal stipend, salary or individual fellowship award.

5. Networking Opportunities

Participants will have the opportunity to connect with:

  • Environmental organizations.
  • Peacebuilding organizations.
  • Youth networks.
  • Community activists.
  • Environmental practitioners.
  • Peacebuilding experts.
  • Trainers and facilitators.
  • Other young people from across Cyprus.

By the end of the programme, participants will become part of the wider UN Youth Champions network, creating opportunities for continued engagement, collaboration and peer learning.

6. Certificate of Participation

Participants who meet the programme requirements may receive a programme certificate.

To receive the certificate, participants must:

  • Attend all four mandatory workshop days.
  • Actively participate in the environmental action process.
  • Fulfil the programme’s participation requirements.

Full compliance with both workshop attendance and environmental action participation is necessary to receive the certificate.

What Will Participants Do During the Workshops?

The workshops will be organized around collaborative learning and practical teamwork.

Participants can expect to take part in activities such as:

  • Interactive sessions on environmental peacebuilding.
  • Discussions with environmental and peacebuilding activists.
  • Presentations from experts and trainers.
  • Group exercises.
  • Team-building activities.
  • Exploration of shared environmental concerns.
  • Development of environmental action ideas.
  • Collaborative project planning.
  • Networking with participants from different communities.

The workshops are designed not only to transfer knowledge but also to help participants develop relationships and learn how to work together across community divisions.

The group work component will be especially important because participants will form teams and develop environmental actions with support from the programme team and experts from across the island.

Implementing Environmental Actions After the Workshops

Following the workshops, each team will be expected to develop its environmental action idea into a simple proposal.

The team will then work toward implementing the action by February 2027.

Potential actions may address shared environmental concerns, although the official announcement does not prescribe a fixed list of project themes. Applicants should therefore remain open to developing practical initiatives that respond to the needs of communities and encourage cooperation.

Examples of possible areas of interest could include:

  • Environmental education.
  • Waste reduction and recycling.
  • Biodiversity conservation.
  • Climate awareness.
  • Sustainable communities.
  • Water conservation.
  • Green public spaces.
  • Environmental volunteering.
  • Sustainable consumption.
  • Community clean-up activities.
  • Nature-based cooperation.
  • Youth-led climate action.

These examples are illustrative rather than an official list of required project topics. The final actions will depend on the ideas developed by selected participants and approved through the programme process.

The organizers encourage actions that reach people across the divide and recommend that initiatives take place throughout Cyprus where possible.

Closing Event in March 2027

The programme will conclude with a closing event expected to take place at the end of March 2027.

All participants are expected to attend the closing event. It will provide an opportunity to reflect on the programme, share experiences, present or discuss environmental actions, celebrate collaboration and recognize the contributions of the Youth Champions.

The closing event may also provide an opportunity for participants to connect with programme partners, environmental organizations, peacebuilding practitioners and other stakeholders.

Programme Location and Attendance Requirements

All programme activities will be held at Ledra Palace, located in the UN buffer zone in Nicosia.

Participation is conditional on applicants being able to enter the UN buffer zone through the relevant crossing points. The official announcement emphasizes that authority over entry through crossing points rests with the respective sides and not with the United Nations.

Applicants must therefore ensure that they possess the required documentation and are able to access the programme venue.

Accommodation Support

Accommodation in Nicosia may be available during the workshop weekends for participants who are unable to commute.

However:

  • Accommodation is subject to demand.
  • Availability is limited.
  • Accommodation is not guaranteed.
  • Arrangements are subject to confirmation.

Applicants who require accommodation should communicate their needs through the application process or with the programme organizers.

Is Participation Free?

Yes. Participation in the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme is free of charge.

However, applicants should carefully review the practical requirements associated with attending the programme, including:

  • Travel to the workshop location.
  • Ability to enter the UN buffer zone.
  • Availability for all workshop dates.
  • Participation in team activities.
  • Ability to contribute to environmental action implementation.
  • Attendance at the closing event.

The announcement confirms that accommodation may be available for some participants, but it does not state that all travel or personal expenses will be covered.

Important Clarification About the Programme

The UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme is a youth development and community engagement initiative. It is not a job, paid internship or full-time employment opportunity.

Participation is:

  • Honorary.
  • Non-remunerated.
  • Not considered employment with the United Nations or British Council.
  • Not associated with UN salaries, emoluments or employment benefits.
  • Not a formal appointment as a UN staff member.

Participants will not receive UN privileges or immunities, and joining the programme does not authorize participants to speak on behalf of the UN, UNFICYP or the British Council.

The programme should therefore be viewed as a learning, leadership, networking and community action opportunity rather than a paid employment placement.

Important Disclaimer for Participants

The views, thoughts and opinions expressed by individuals or groups designated as UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace are expressed in their personal capacity.

These views do not necessarily represent the official views of:

  • The United Nations.
  • UNFICYP.
  • The British Council.
  • Their officials or personnel.

Participants should therefore understand that being selected as a Youth Champion does not mean they are official spokespersons for the United Nations or UNFICYP.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme 2026 is:

20 September 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their forms before the deadline. The official announcement indicates that successful applicants are expected to be notified by 23 September 2026.

Late applications may not be considered, so applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to complete and submit the form.

How to Apply for the UN Youth Champions Programme

Interested applicants should complete the Official Online Application Form before the deadline.

Application Steps

  1. Review the eligibility criteria carefully.
  2. Confirm that you are aged 18–30 and living in Cyprus.
  3. Ensure that you can attend all four workshop days.
  4. Confirm that you can participate in environmental action activities through February 2027.
  5. Ensure that you have a very good knowledge of English.
  6. Check that you have not previously participated in a UN Youth Champions programme.
  7. Complete the online application form.
  8. Submit the application by 20 September 2026.

Official Application Form

Interested applicants can apply through the official application form:

Apply for the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme

Official Programme Information

For the original announcement and additional information, visit:

UNFICYP: Apply Now to Become a UN Youth Champion for Environment and Peace

Contact Information

For questions about the programme or application process, applicants can contact:

Email: unficyp-youthchampions@un.org

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although the announcement does not provide a detailed scoring rubric, applicants can improve their applications by clearly demonstrating their motivation and readiness to participate.

A strong application should communicate:

1. Genuine Interest in Environmental Issues

Explain why environmental sustainability, climate action, conservation or related issues matter to you.

Applicants do not need extensive technical knowledge, but they should demonstrate curiosity and a willingness to learn.

2. Commitment to Peacebuilding

Describe your interest in dialogue, community cooperation, social cohesion or building relationships across differences.

The programme is specifically designed to bring together participants from different communities, so applicants should show that they value respect, inclusion and collaboration.

3. Willingness to Work in Teams

The programme requires participants to develop environmental actions as part of a team. Applicants should be prepared to listen, contribute ideas, manage differences and work toward shared goals.

4. Availability for All Programme Activities

Applicants should confirm that they can attend the workshops on:

  • 3 October 2026.
  • 4 October 2026.
  • 10 October 2026.
  • 11 October 2026.

They should also be able to participate in the environmental action implementation process and attend the closing event in March 2027.

5. Interest in Practical Action

The programme is not limited to discussions or classroom learning. Participants will be expected to develop and implement an environmental action.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate a willingness to move from learning to practical community engagement.

6. Understanding of the Programme’s Requirements

Applicants should understand that:

  • Participation is free.
  • The programme is not paid employment.
  • Attendance is mandatory.
  • Environmental actions must be implemented by February 2027.
  • Entry into the UN buffer zone is the participant’s responsibility.
  • Accommodation in Nicosia may be limited and is not guaranteed.
  • A certificate depends on full compliance with programme requirements.

Why This Programme Matters

The UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme responds to two closely connected challenges: environmental sustainability and peaceful coexistence.

Environmental problems do not stop at community boundaries. Climate change, pollution, waste, biodiversity loss and resource pressures can affect people across social and political divisions. Cooperation on these issues can help communities identify common interests and develop practical solutions.

The programme also recognizes the role of young people as contributors to peacebuilding. Rather than treating youth only as beneficiaries, it gives them opportunities to:

  • Develop leadership skills.
  • Participate in decision-making.
  • Build relationships across communities.
  • Design community initiatives.
  • Strengthen environmental awareness.
  • Contribute to sustainable development.
  • Become involved in peacebuilding processes.

By combining environmental action with intercommunal cooperation, the initiative seeks to show how shared goals can help build trust and strengthen social cohesion.

Visit HERE to learn more about the UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace 2026.

Conclusion

The UN Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme 2026 offers young people living in Cyprus an opportunity to gain knowledge, build cross-community relationships and develop practical environmental initiatives that contribute to peace and sustainability.

Organized by UNFICYP in partnership with the British Council, the programme includes immersive workshops, team-based project development, mentoring, small grants for environmental actions and networking with environmental and peacebuilding practitioners.

The programme is open to individuals aged 18 to 30 from any community living in Cyprus. Previous experience in environmental peacebuilding is not required, but applicants must demonstrate motivation, a strong interest in environmental and peace-related issues, good English-language skills and a commitment to attending all workshops and participating in environmental action implementation.

Participation is free, but the programme is honorary and non-remunerated. Applicants must also be able to access the UN buffer zone in Nicosia, where activities will take place.

The application deadline is 20 September 2026. Eligible young people who are passionate about environmental sustainability, peacebuilding, youth leadership and community cooperation are encouraged to apply early and take part in this opportunity to help build a more peaceful and sustainable Cyprus.

item.content:encoded:
The Australian Permanent Mission to the United Nations and International Organisations in Vienna is offering a valuable 5–6 month traineeship in Vienna, Austria, for Australians interested in international relations, multilateral diplomacy, international organisations, security, nuclear issues, drugs and crime, and international affairs.

The traineeship provides participants with the opportunity to gain first-hand experience working within a busy Australian overseas mission while supporting Australia’s engagement with Vienna-based multilateral organisations.

Participants will work under the guidance and mentorship of Australian diplomats and will have opportunities to develop practical skills in research, reporting, program development, public diplomacy, digital communication, meeting support, and international engagement.

The program is expected to offer two traineeships in 2027.

The application deadline is 22 September 2026.

Australian DFAT Vienna Traineeship 2027 Overview

  • Opportunity: DFAT Vienna Traineeship
  • Department: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
  • Organisation: Commonwealth Government of Australia
  • Location: Australian Embassy, Vienna, Austria
  • Address: The Icon, Gertrude-Fröehlich-Sandner-Str. 2, Vienna 1100, Austria
  • Duration: Approximately 5–6 months
  • Expected intake: 2027
  • Number of traineeships: Two traineeships are envisaged
  • Workplace type: Onsite
  • Compensation: EUR 1,523.15 per month
  • Employment type: Internship/traineeship
  • Application deadline: 22 September 2026
  • Nationality requirement: Australian citizenship is mandatory

About the Australian Permanent Mission in Vienna

The Australian Permanent Mission to the United Nations and International Organisations in Vienna undertakes a broad range of multilateral diplomatic functions.

The Mission is accredited to several major international organisations based in Vienna, including:

  • International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
  • Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization (CTBTO)
  • United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)
  • Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)

The Permanent Mission is co-located with the Australian Embassy in Vienna. The Embassy is responsible for Australia’s bilateral relations with Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary, Slovakia and Slovenia.

This makes the traineeship particularly relevant for people seeking practical exposure to both multilateral diplomacy and Australia’s broader international engagement.

About the DFAT Vienna Traineeship

The traineeship is designed to provide participants with practical experience supporting Australia’s interests at the international level.

Successful trainees will work under the guidance of experienced officers and Australian diplomats.

The experience is intended to provide exposure to how an overseas diplomatic mission operates and how Australia engages with international organisations and other stakeholders.

The traineeship covers a particularly busy period in the calendar of Vienna-based multilateral organisations, including major meetings concerning nuclear issues and transnational crime.

Participants may therefore gain first-hand exposure to international meetings, diplomatic processes, research, reporting, public diplomacy, and stakeholder engagement.

What Will Trainees Do?

The role involves a range of research, administrative, communications, diplomatic-support, and program-related responsibilities.

Potential duties include, but are not limited to, the following.

1. Support Multilateral Meetings and Conferences

Trainees may assist with the preparation for and attendance at multilateral meetings and conferences.

Responsibilities can include:

  • Preparing for meetings
  • Attending relevant meetings
  • Taking notes
  • Supporting meeting documentation
  • Contributing to the drafting of reports
  • Helping officers follow up on relevant issues

This provides trainees with an opportunity to understand how international meetings are prepared for and documented.

2. Conduct Research and Present Information

Trainees may support research and the presentation of information concerning:

  • Multilateral issues
  • Bilateral issues
  • Public diplomacy
  • International affairs
  • Other issues relevant to Australia’s interests

This component can help participants strengthen their analytical, research, writing, and information-presentation skills.

3. Support Official Visits

The traineeship may involve assisting with preparations for official visits and contributing to program development.

This can include supporting the planning and organisation of activities involving Australian officials and international stakeholders.

4. Digital Communication

Trainees may contribute to content development for the Permanent Mission’s digital platforms.

Potential channels include:

  • The Permanent Mission’s website
  • X (formerly Twitter)
  • LinkedIn
  • Facebook

This means applicants with strong writing, digital communication, social media, and content-development skills may find this component particularly relevant.

5. Outreach and Events

Trainees may also support engagement and outreach activities and contribute to Mission events.

This provides exposure to public diplomacy and stakeholder engagement in an international setting.

Skills You Can Develop

The traineeship offers the opportunity to develop a broad range of professional skills.

These include:

  • International relations research
  • Multilateral diplomacy
  • Policy research
  • Analytical thinking
  • Report writing
  • Meeting documentation
  • Program development
  • Public diplomacy
  • Digital communication
  • Strategic thinking
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • Event support
  • Teamwork
  • Organisation
  • Problem-solving
  • Working under pressure

Participants will also gain practical insight into the operation of an Australian diplomatic mission overseas.

Who Is the Australian Government Looking For?

The Mission is looking for an undergraduate or postgraduate student or recent graduate with an enthusiasm for multilateralism and international affairs.

Candidates should have relevant education and abilities that can contribute to advancing Australia’s national interests.

Preference is given to applicants who have recently completed, or who have completed at least four semesters of tertiary studies, in relevant areas.

These areas include:

  • Political science
  • International relations
  • International law
  • International security
  • Defence studies
  • Science and technology

Prior exposure to, or demonstrated knowledge of, the United Nations system is highly desirable.

The opportunity may therefore be particularly suitable for students and recent graduates seeking to establish a career in:

  • Diplomacy
  • International relations
  • Foreign affairs
  • International organisations
  • Government
  • International security
  • Public diplomacy
  • Multilateral affairs
  • Policy research

Personal Qualities and Professional Skills

Beyond academic qualifications, DFAT is seeking candidates who demonstrate strong professional and interpersonal qualities.

Applicants should be:

Highly Motivated

Candidates should demonstrate enthusiasm for international affairs and a commitment to contributing to Australia’s national interests.

Strong Communicators

Excellent oral and written communication skills are expected.

This is particularly important because the traineeship involves research, reporting, meetings, stakeholder engagement, and digital communication.

Strategic Thinkers

Applicants should demonstrate the ability to analyse situations, identify relevant issues, and think strategically.

Practical Problem-Solvers

The Mission is seeking people who can approach challenges constructively and identify practical solutions.

Team Players

The role involves working with diplomats, officers, other staff, international organisations, and external stakeholders.

Good teamwork and organisational skills are therefore important.

Flexible and Adaptable

The environment of an overseas diplomatic mission can involve changing priorities and time-sensitive activities.

Applicants should be flexible, adaptable, resourceful, and able to work under pressure.

Respectful and Ethical

Applicants should demonstrate respect for others, ethical conduct, and an appreciation of diversity.

Mandatory Eligibility Requirements

Before applying, candidates should carefully check the mandatory eligibility criteria.

Australian Citizenship

Applicants must be Australian citizens.

This is explicitly stated as a mandatory requirement.

Non-Australian citizens are therefore not eligible for this particular traineeship.

Right to Work in Austria

Successful applicants must obtain, or be able to obtain, an appropriate visa giving them the right to work in Austria for the duration of the traineeship.

Relevant Qualifications and Background

Applicants must possess relevant qualifications and background.

Preference is given to candidates who have completed, or are currently completing, tertiary studies in areas such as:

  • Political science
  • International relations
  • International law
  • International security
  • Defence studies
  • Science and technology

Interest in Multilateralism

Applicants must demonstrate a genuine interest in multilateralism.

It is not enough simply to state an interest; candidates should be able to demonstrate this interest through their academic background, experience, activities, or responses to the application questionnaire.

Police Check

Successful applicants must be willing to undergo a mandatory police check.

Relocation to Vienna

Applicants must be willing to relocate to Vienna, Austria, for a period of up to six months.

The relocation is primarily self-funded.

This means trainees are responsible for arrangements and costs associated with:

  • Travel
  • Visa
  • Passport
  • Accommodation
  • Health insurance

Applicants should therefore consider the financial implications of living in Vienna before applying.

Financial Support and Monthly Stipend

The traineeship is funded and provides a monthly stipend of:

EUR 1,523.15 per month

However, applicants should note that the traineeship’s relocation requirements are primarily self-funded.

The stipend therefore needs to be considered alongside the personal costs associated with relocating to and living in Vienna, including accommodation, travel, visa-related expenses, passport costs, and health insurance.

Working Hours

The Mission’s office hours are:

08:30–16:30, Monday to Friday

UN meetings are usually held between:

10:00–18:00

Trainees should therefore expect a professional working environment connected to the schedules of the Mission and Vienna-based international organisations.

Conduct and Ethics

The Australian Permanent Mission expects high standards of professional conduct from its staff and trainees.

Ethical behaviour is considered important not only for the effective operation of the workplace but also for maintaining the reputation and standing of the Mission and its employees in Australia and internationally.

Trainees participating in the program will be required to comply with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Locally Engaged Staff Code of Conduct.

The Code takes into account the particular responsibilities associated with representing Australia outside the country.

Application Documents

Applicants must submit several documents as part of their application.

1. Resume

Applicants should submit a resume of no more than two pages.

The resume should clearly communicate the applicant’s:

  • Education
  • Relevant experience
  • Skills
  • Achievements
  • Research experience
  • International affairs interests
  • Other relevant qualifications

Because the resume is limited to two pages, applicants should prioritise information directly relevant to the traineeship.

2. Written Reference

A written reference must be included with the application.

Applicants should select a referee who can provide meaningful evidence of their academic, professional, research, communication, teamwork, or other relevant abilities.

3. University Letter of Support

A letter of support from the applicant’s university is optional but encouraged where appropriate.

Students may therefore wish to explore whether their university can provide an appropriate supporting letter.

4. Traineeship Questionnaire

Applicants must complete a questionnaire designed to assess their suitability for the position.

The questionnaire evaluates qualities, experience, skills, and knowledge relevant to working as a trainee at the Mission.

Questionnaire Questions

Applicants are asked to respond to six questions.

Each response should be no more than 150 words.

Question 1: Motivation

Applicants must explain:

Why are you applying for this traineeship?

This response should clearly communicate the applicant’s motivation and demonstrate why the opportunity fits their academic and career interests.

Question 2: International Relations and DFAT

Applicants must:

  • Explain their interest in international relations.
  • Demonstrate their understanding of the work and goals of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

Applicants should therefore research DFAT and understand its role before completing the questionnaire.

Question 3: Analytical and Research Skills

Applicants must briefly describe a recent:

  • Achievement
  • Project
  • Task

that demonstrates their:

  • Analytical skills
  • Research skills
  • Strategic thinking

A strong response should provide a specific example rather than simply listing skills.

Question 4: Teamwork

Applicants must demonstrate their ability to:

  • Work effectively as part of a team
  • Build strong working relationships

Applicants should use a concrete example where possible.

Question 5: Problem-Solving Under Pressure

Applicants must demonstrate their ability to solve problems under pressure.

A practical example from university, employment, volunteering, research, leadership, or another relevant setting can be used.

Question 6: Additional Languages

Applicants may optionally state whether they speak languages other than English.

This question is optional.

Cover Letter Is Not Required

An important point for applicants is that cover letters are not required.

The announcement specifically states that cover letters will not be considered as part of the application.

Applicants should therefore focus their effort on preparing:

  • A strong two-page resume
  • A written reference
  • A university support letter where appropriate
  • Strong questionnaire responses

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the DFAT Vienna traineeship is:

22 September 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow sufficient time to prepare the required documents and questionnaire responses.

Where Is the Traineeship Based?

The traineeship is based at the:

Australian Embassy, Vienna

The listed address is:

The Icon
Gertrude-Fröehlich-Sandner-Str. 2
Vienna 1100
Austria

The workplace type is listed as onsite.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This traineeship may be particularly relevant to Australian students and recent graduates interested in international careers.

Strong prospective applicants may include students or recent graduates studying:

  1. Political science
  2. International relations
  3. International law
  4. International security
  5. Defence studies
  6. Science and technology
  7. Other closely related fields

Candidates with knowledge of the UN system may have an additional advantage.

The opportunity may also appeal to people interested in developing careers in:

  • Australian foreign affairs
  • Diplomacy
  • International organisations
  • Multilateral institutions
  • Public diplomacy
  • International security
  • Government policy
  • International development
  • Global affairs
  • Research and analysis
  • Strategic communications

Important Financial Considerations

Although the traineeship provides a monthly stipend of EUR 1,523.15, candidates should carefully consider the financial requirements associated with relocating to Vienna.

The announcement states that relocation is primarily self-funded, including:

  • Travel costs
  • Visa costs
  • Passport costs
  • Accommodation
  • Health insurance

Applicants should therefore assess their ability to cover these costs for the duration of the traineeship.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Why This Traineeship Is Valuable

The DFAT Vienna traineeship provides more than classroom-based exposure to international relations.

Participants can gain practical experience within an actual diplomatic mission and work alongside experienced Australian diplomats.

The combination of research, reporting, international meetings, public diplomacy, digital communication, program development, outreach, and stakeholder engagement can provide a broad understanding of how Australia’s international interests are represented and advanced overseas.

The location is also significant because Vienna hosts several major international organisations, including the IAEA, CTBTO, UNODC and OSCE.

For someone considering a future career in diplomacy or international affairs, exposure to these institutions can provide valuable professional experience.

About the Commonwealth Government of Australia

The Commonwealth Government of Australia employs staff overseas to support the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade and other Australian Government agencies at overseas posts, including:

  • Embassies
  • High commissions
  • Consulates

Locally Engaged Staff support and complement Australian Public Service employees by providing important in-country knowledge, skills, networks, and continuity.

The Australian Government’s overseas workforce operates across more than 100 locations and contributes to Australia’s international objectives and national interests.

The Human Resources Section based at the Australian High Commission in London manages local job vacancies across the European region, including various categories of employment and internship programs.

Conclusion

The Australian Permanent Mission to the United Nations and International Organisations in Vienna DFAT Traineeship 2027 is a practical international-affairs opportunity for Australian undergraduate or postgraduate students and recent graduates seeking experience in diplomacy, multilateralism, international organisations, public diplomacy, research, and government.

The traineeship offers an opportunity to work within a diplomatic mission, receive mentorship from Australian diplomats, participate in activities connected to Vienna-based multilateral organisations, and develop skills in research, reporting, program development, digital communication, public diplomacy, and stakeholder engagement.

The application deadline is 22 September 2026.

For Australian students and recent graduates who want to gain practical experience in multilateral diplomacy and international affairs, this traineeship offers an opportunity to gain direct exposure to the work of an Australian overseas mission and the international organisations based in Vienna.

Click HERE for more internship opportunities.
