item.content:encoded:
DoSomething is inviting passionate young people across the United States to apply for its inaugural DoCrew, a unique paid leadership opportunity designed for emerging young adult leaders who want to use their voices, experiences, creativity, and personal stories to inspire others to take action on issues that matter to their communities and generation.

The DoCrew will bring together four young leaders who will become part of DoSomething’s efforts to engage young people around important social issues. Selected members will represent different areas of focus, create content for DoSomething’s digital platforms, share their perspectives, participate in leadership and media development activities, and encourage other young people to get involved in causes they care about.

Unlike opportunities that require applicants to already be famous influencers, professional content creators, or nationally recognized activists, the DoCrew is designed to give authentic young people an opportunity to tell their stories and demonstrate how they are making a difference.

Most importantly, this is a paid opportunity. Each selected DoCrew member will receive $250 every two weeks, subject to applicable tax and legal requirements, for successfully completing the agreed responsibilities during the six-month pilot.

Applications are currently open, and interested applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline.

About the DoCrew

The DoCrew is a new initiative from DoSomething focused on identifying and supporting emerging young leaders who can help demonstrate what youth leadership and civic participation look like in everyday life.

DoSomething believes that taking action does not necessarily mean leading a major national movement or having thousands of followers. Young people can make a difference through the choices they make, the issues they care about, the communities they support, and the ways they encourage others to participate.

The inaugural DoCrew will consist of four selected young people. Each member will represent one of four areas connected to DoSomething’s broader mission.

As a DoCrew member, participants will have the opportunity to:

  • Represent an issue or cause that is important to them.
  • Create social media content for DoSomething.
  • Share personal perspectives and experiences.
  • Highlight issues affecting young people and their communities.
  • Encourage other young people to take meaningful action.
  • Develop their storytelling and communication abilities.
  • Work directly with DoSomething staff.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and virtual meetings.
  • Contribute to campaigns and media opportunities.
  • Build a portfolio of published content and campaign work.
  • Become part of a small community of four emerging changemakers.
  • Help shape how DoSomething engages with its members.

The Four DoCrew Focus Areas

Applicants will have the opportunity to connect their interests and experiences to one of four DoSomething focus areas.

1. Walk the Walk

This area focuses on:

  • Equity
  • Justice
  • Economic mobility
  • Belonging
  • Community service

Applicants who are passionate about creating more equitable communities, improving access to opportunities, supporting marginalized communities, or encouraging young people to serve others may find this area particularly relevant.

2. No Planet B

This focus area is centered on:

  • Climate action
  • Sustainability
  • Environmental justice

Young people who care about climate change, environmental protection, sustainability, environmental inequality, conservation, or encouraging communities to take environmental action can connect their experiences to this pillar.

3. Thrive On

This area focuses on:

  • Mental health
  • Safety
  • Wellbeing

Applicants can use this area to highlight their interest in creating safer and healthier communities and supporting young people in areas related to wellbeing and safety.

4. Be Heard

This pillar focuses on:

  • Community voice
  • Democracy
  • Advocacy
  • Civic participation

Young people interested in civic engagement, democratic participation, advocacy, community organizing, public issues, or encouraging others to make their voices heard may be particularly suited to this focus area.

What Will DoCrew Members Do?

Selected members will play an active role in helping DoSomething communicate with and inspire its community of young people.

Their responsibilities will include creating and submitting digital content, participating in virtual meetings and coaching sessions, responding to feedback, supporting campaigns, and sharing reflections about their experiences.

The content may include:

  • Short-form videos
  • Photos
  • Social media posts
  • Written reflections
  • Blog-style content
  • Campaign-related materials
  • Other approved digital storytelling

DoCrew members will also have their content reviewed according to DoSomething’s content review process and applicable organizational guidelines.

This means successful applicants should be comfortable communicating their ideas publicly and working collaboratively with an organization to develop content.

Do You Need to Be an Influencer?

No.

One of the notable features of the DoCrew opportunity is that applicants do not need to be professional influencers, content creators, or nationally recognized activists.

DoSomething is looking for authentic young people with:

  • Genuine stories
  • Strong ideas
  • Personal perspectives
  • Curiosity
  • Initiative
  • Community involvement
  • A willingness to learn
  • An interest in inspiring others

The organization is interested in discovering young leaders whose contributions may not already be publicly recognized.

Therefore, applicants should focus on demonstrating who they are, what they care about, what they have done, and what they could inspire others to do.

Benefits of Joining the DoCrew

Selected participants will receive several professional and personal development benefits in addition to financial compensation.

Leadership and Media Training

DoCrew members will receive leadership and media training designed to strengthen their ability to communicate ideas, tell stories, advocate for causes, and engage audiences.

National Platform

Members will have an opportunity to share their voices with DoSomething’s community of more than 1 million members.

This provides an opportunity for emerging leaders to gain exposure and communicate their ideas on a significant national platform.

Hands-On Content Creation Experience

Participants will gain practical experience creating different forms of digital content, potentially including:

  • Social media content
  • Videos
  • Blogs
  • Campaign materials
  • Written reflections

This experience could be particularly valuable for applicants interested in communications, advocacy, social media, public relations, nonprofit work, digital storytelling, or community engagement.

One-on-One Mentorship

Selected members will receive mentorship and ongoing support from the DoSomething team.

This can provide participants with guidance as they develop their leadership, communication, and storytelling skills.

Paid Leadership Experience

The DoCrew is not simply a volunteer position.

Each selected member will receive $250 every two weeks, subject to tax and legal requirements, for successfully completing the agreed responsibilities during the six-month pilot.

Portfolio Development

Participants will have the opportunity to build a portfolio through published content and campaign work.

This may be useful when applying for future leadership programs, jobs, fellowships, internships, communications roles, nonprofit positions, or other opportunities requiring evidence of practical experience.

Community of Changemakers

The inaugural cohort will consist of only four young leaders, giving members an opportunity to work closely with other passionate individuals.

Opportunity to Influence DoSomething’s Engagement

DoCrew members will contribute their perspectives and experiences to help shape how DoSomething engages with its members and communicates with young people.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet several requirements to be considered for the DoCrew.

Applicants must:

  1. Be at least 18 years of age when the DoCrew term begins in October 2026.
  2. Live in the United States.
  3. Be a current DoSomething member or create a free DoSomething account before applying.
  4. Be available to actively participate as a DoCrew member.
  5. Be available for the virtual orientation scheduled for Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET.
  6. Be available to participate in regular virtual check-ins.
  7. Be willing to create short-form digital content.
  8. Be comfortable creating videos, photos, written reflections, and social media posts.
  9. Be comfortable having approved content shared through DoSomething’s website, social media, email, fundraising materials, and other communications.
  10. Demonstrate a meaningful connection to at least one DoSomething pillar or civic engagement.
  11. Agree to follow DoSomething’s community standards.
  12. Follow the organization’s brand guidelines and content review process.
  13. Have reliable access to a smartphone or another device capable of recording video.
  14. Have access to a device capable of participating in virtual meetings.
  15. Be willing to comply with DoSomething’s applicable policies and guidelines.
  16. Comply with policies concerning confidentiality, privacy, social media, intellectual property, appropriate online conduct, and use of the organization’s name.
  17. Complete all required application, consent, and participation documents.
  18. Complete the required agreement before beginning the program.
  19. Be legally eligible to work in the United States.

Who Is DoSomething Looking For?

DoSomething is looking for emerging young adult leaders who have authentic stories, strong ideas, and a genuine desire to make a difference.

Applicants do not need to be famous or have thousands of social media followers.

Strong candidates may demonstrate:

  • A meaningful connection to a particular social issue.
  • Community involvement.
  • Curiosity about important issues.
  • Initiative and willingness to take action.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Storytelling potential.
  • Reliability.
  • Willingness to learn.
  • Ability to collaborate with others.
  • A desire to inspire other young people.

Applicants whose leadership may not always receive public recognition are encouraged to apply.

Time Commitment

DoCrew members should expect to spend approximately 15 to 20 hours per month participating in the program.

This time may be spent on:

  • Creating and submitting content.
  • Participating in virtual meetings.
  • Participating in coaching sessions.
  • Responding to content feedback.
  • Supporting occasional DoSomething campaigns.
  • Participating in media opportunities.
  • Sharing reflections about the DoCrew experience.

Specific deadlines and expectations will be communicated before selected members formally accept their positions.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they have sufficient time to meet the program’s requirements.

Compensation

The DoCrew is a paid leadership opportunity.

Each selected DoCrew member will receive:

$250 every two weeks

The payment is subject to applicable tax and legal requirements.

The compensation is provided for successfully completing the agreed responsibilities of the six-month pilot.

Applicants should therefore understand that the stipend is connected to fulfilling the responsibilities associated with the program.

Selection Process

Applications will be evaluated based on several factors.

DoSomething will consider:

  • Connection to the selected pillar.
  • Authenticity and clarity.
  • Evidence of curiosity.
  • Initiative.
  • Community involvement.
  • Storytelling potential.
  • Reliability.
  • Readiness to participate.
  • Willingness to learn.
  • Ability to collaborate.
  • Diversity of experiences.
  • Diversity of perspectives.
  • Diversity of locations.
  • Diversity of leadership styles.

The final selection will also consider the overall diversity of the four-person DoCrew cohort.

If selected as a finalist, an applicant may be invited to participate in a virtual interview before the final four DoCrew members are selected.

Commitment to Inclusion

DoSomething states that it is committed to creating an inclusive DoCrew.

Young people from historically underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

The organization also encourages applicants whose leadership may not always be publicly recognized.

Selection decisions will be made in accordance with applicable law and DoSomething’s nondiscrimination policies.

Program Timeline

The DoCrew term is expected to begin in October 2026.

The program information states that the DoCrew experience will run from October 2026 to October 2027. However, the compensation section refers specifically to a six-month pilot.

Applicants should carefully review the official program information and any agreement provided by DoSomething for the final details concerning the duration and responsibilities of the pilot.

Virtual Orientation

The required virtual orientation is scheduled for:

Saturday, October 10, 2026

Time: 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM ET

Applicants should make sure they are available during this period if selected.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the inaugural DoCrew is:

September 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should complete the official DoCrew application through DoSomething.

Before applying, applicants should ensure that they meet all eligibility requirements and have considered which of the four DoSomething pillars best reflects their interests and experiences.

Applicants should use their application to clearly communicate:

  • Who they are.
  • What they care about.
  • The issues that matter to them.
  • What they have done in their community.
  • What they have learned from their experiences.
  • Why their chosen DoSomething pillar matters to them.
  • How they could use their voice to inspire others.
  • Why they would be a strong addition to the inaugural DoCrew.

Applicants should also ensure that all required information and documents are submitted before the deadline.

Apply Here

Official DoCrew application:

http://dosomething.org/application/docrew

Official Website: DoSomething DoCrew 

For more leadership programs visit the OFY Website HERE

Why This Opportunity Is Worth Considering

The DoSomething DoCrew offers an opportunity to combine youth leadership, advocacy, digital storytelling, professional development, mentorship, and paid participation.

For young people interested in areas such as nonprofit organizations, social impact, communications, public relations, advocacy, community development, civic engagement, environmental issues, youth leadership, or digital media, the experience could provide valuable practical exposure.

The opportunity may also be particularly attractive to young people who have strong personal stories and community experiences but do not have a large online following.

DoSomething specifically states that applicants do not need to be influencers or nationally recognized activists. Instead, the organization wants to hear what applicants do and what they could inspire others to do.

Conclusion

The inaugural DoSomething DoCrew is an opportunity for four emerging young adult leaders in the United States to use their voices, experiences, and creativity to encourage other young people to take action.

Selected members will represent one of four focus areas: Walk the Walk, No Planet B, Thrive On, or Be Heard. They will create digital content, participate in leadership and media training, receive mentorship, work with DoSomething staff, contribute to campaigns, build their portfolios, and connect with other young changemakers.

The opportunity also provides financial compensation, with each selected member receiving $250 every two weeks, subject to applicable tax and legal requirements, for successfully completing the agreed responsibilities of the six-month pilot.

Applicants do not need to be influencers, professional content creators, or nationally recognized activists. DoSomething is looking for authentic young people with strong ideas, meaningful experiences, curiosity, initiative, and the ability to inspire others.

Eligible applicants should carefully review the requirements, prepare a compelling application, and submit it before the deadline.

The application deadline is September 22, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST.

If you are a young person in the United States who is passionate about making a difference and believes your voice can inspire others to take action, the DoCrew could provide an opportunity to turn that passion into meaningful leadership experience.

item.content:encoded:
The Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program (PHIFP), offered by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), is now accepting applications for its Class of 2027. The program provides an advanced professional development opportunity for qualified individuals who want to apply computer science, data science, information technology, statistics, epidemiology, engineering, and related expertise to real-world public health challenges.

The fellowship combines intensive practical experience with structured coursework, allowing participants to work on public health informatics projects while developing specialized skills that can contribute to stronger health information systems and improved population health outcomes.

For professionals interested in the intersection of public health, technology, data analytics, information systems, and health research, the CDC PHIFP offers an opportunity to gain substantial hands-on experience through a two-year, full-time fellowship.

The Class of 2027 application period opened on September 1, 2026, and closes on November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. Applicants should ensure that all required application materials are submitted before the deadline because late applications will not be accepted.

About the Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program

Public health informatics focuses on the systematic use of information, technology, data, and information systems to improve population-level health outcomes.

The CDC describes PHIFP fellows as “data detectives” because their work involves applying technical and analytical expertise to public health problems. Fellows work with systems that capture, manage, analyze, and use information to support public health decision-making and operations. The fellowship is designed for professionals who already possess relevant academic and professional experience and want to further develop their ability to use technology and data to solve complex public health problems.

During the fellowship, participants are assigned to host sites within CDC and work on advanced projects involving public health information systems and data. At the same time, fellows receive opportunities for classroom and experiential learning, enabling them to strengthen both their technical and public health competencies.

What Makes the CDC PHIFP Fellowship Different?

PHIFP is structured as a two-year paid fellowship focused on applying information science and technology to public health practice. Rather than being limited to classroom-based study, the program emphasizes practical experience within CDC.

The fellowship combines:

  • On-the-job professional training
  • Coursework in public health informatics, data science, and public health
  • Public health information-system projects
  • Informatics evaluations
  • Technical assistance activities
  • Research and development work
  • A capstone project
  • Collaboration with public health professionals and organizations

The program’s training model consists of approximately 90% on-the-job training and 10% coursework, making practical experience a major component of the fellowship.

What Do PHIFP Fellows Do?

Fellows are placed in Centers, Institutes, and Offices across the CDC, where they participate in experiential training and contribute to projects designed to strengthen the agency’s informatics capacity.

The work can involve solving complex public health problems through computer science, data science, information technology, and informatics.

Depending on their assignment, fellows may participate in activities such as:

1. Developing Public Health Information Systems

Fellows may contribute to the design, development, implementation, enhancement, or evaluation of information systems used in public health.

This provides practical exposure to how technology can be developed and adapted to support public health programs and decision-making.

2. Conducting Informatics Evaluations

Participants may evaluate complex public health information systems to determine how effectively they meet their intended objectives.

These activities can involve assessing systems, identifying opportunities for improvement, and contributing technical recommendations.

3. Supporting Public Health Research and Development

PHIFP fellows work with teams involved in the research and development of public health information systems. This allows participants to apply their academic and technical knowledge to projects with real-world public health applications.

4. Providing Technical Assistance

Fellows can provide short-term technical assistance to federal, international, state, local, and territorial health departments as well as nonprofit organizations through special assignments known as Info-Aids.

This component can expose fellows to a variety of public health environments and information-system challenges.

5. Contributing to Emergency Response

PHIFP fellows may also contribute to CDC emergency response activities. This demonstrates how informatics, technology, and data can support public health operations during urgent situations.

6. Completing a Capstone Project

As part of their fellowship requirements, fellows complete a capstone project involving the design, development, implementation, enhancement, or evaluation of an information system or other informatics artifact within the public health domain.

The capstone provides an opportunity to demonstrate the skills developed throughout the fellowship.

Training and Learning Structure

The PHIFP fellowship provides competency-based training over two years.

The program is particularly suitable for professionals who want to move beyond theoretical knowledge and develop the ability to apply technical expertise to practical public health challenges.

The training structure includes:

  • Practical assignments at CDC host sites
  • Informatics and data science coursework
  • Public health learning
  • Technical projects
  • Collaboration with multidisciplinary teams
  • Informatics evaluation
  • Information-system development and improvement
  • Short-term technical assistance
  • Capstone project development

Before beginning their regular assignments, selected fellows must complete a two-week orientation. The orientation introduces fellows to CDC, public health, and the role of informatics within the public health system.

Academic Backgrounds Relevant to PHIFP

The fellowship is designed for applicants with advanced academic qualifications in fields that can contribute to public health informatics.

Eligible qualifying degrees can include doctoral-level degrees such as:

  • PhD
  • MD
  • PharmD
  • DrPH
  • Equivalent doctoral degrees

Applicants may also qualify through master’s-level degrees such as:

  • MPH
  • MS
  • MSc
  • Equivalent master’s degrees

The qualifying degree must be in an approved field, including public health, medicine, healthcare, health services research, computer science, data science, medical or public health informatics, statistics, epidemiology, engineering, or operations research. (CDC)

Professional and Research Experience

Academic qualifications alone are not the only consideration.

Applicants must also have at least one year of documented full-time work or volunteer experience in the same field as their qualifying degree. This requirement is intended to ensure that candidates have practical exposure to their area of specialization before entering the fellowship.

Applicants should also document relevant research or evaluation experience completed during or after their academic training.

Examples of acceptable research experience include:

  • Academic publications
  • Thesis writing and defense
  • Poster presentations
  • Research proposals
  • Evaluation proposals
  • Other relevant research or evaluation activities

Candidates should therefore ensure that their application clearly demonstrates not only their academic background but also their practical and research experience.

Fellowship Commitment and Work Arrangement

PHIFP is a two-year, full-time fellowship. Applicants must be prepared to make this commitment if selected.

An important consideration for prospective applicants is that the fellowship is not a remote program.

Selected fellows must relocate to their assigned CDC site. According to the CDC, approximately 85% of assignments are in Atlanta, Georgia, while about 10% are in Washington, DC. Relocation costs are not paid by the program.

Applicants should therefore consider their ability to relocate and work on-site before applying.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The PHIFP opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals who want to build careers at the intersection of technology and public health.

Potential applicants may include professionals with backgrounds in:

  • Public health
  • Medicine
  • Healthcare
  • Health services research
  • Public health informatics
  • Medical informatics
  • Computer science
  • Data science
  • Statistics
  • Epidemiology
  • Engineering
  • Operations research

The program can be particularly valuable for individuals who want to use technical and analytical skills to address health-system challenges and improve how public health organizations collect, manage, analyze, and use information.

Key Benefits of the Fellowship

Although the fellowship is primarily a professional training opportunity, its structure provides several significant career-development advantages.

Practical Public Health Experience

Fellows gain direct experience working on public health informatics projects rather than relying exclusively on classroom learning.

Advanced Data and Technology Exposure

Participants can apply computer science, data science, information technology, and analytical skills to real-world public health challenges.

Experience Within CDC

Fellows are assigned to CDC host sites and work alongside professionals involved in public health programs, information systems, research, and related activities.

Structured Professional Development

The two-year competency-based structure provides fellows with a combination of experiential learning and coursework.

Exposure to Diverse Public Health Challenges

Through host-site projects, technical assistance assignments, informatics evaluations, and other activities, fellows can gain experience addressing different types of public health information and technology challenges.

Development of a Professional Portfolio

Projects completed during the fellowship, including the capstone project, can provide valuable evidence of practical expertise in public health informatics.

Contribution to Public Health Systems

The program is not solely focused on individual professional development. Fellows contribute their technical expertise to projects intended to strengthen public health information systems and support public health organizations.

Application Timeline for the PHIFP Class of 2027

Applicants should pay close attention to the official timeline.

Stage Date
Application opens September 1, 2026
Application deadline November 6, 2026
Recommendation Forms deadline November 15, 2026
Application screening November 2026–January 2027
Host-site interviews January–February 2027
Final selections February–March 2027
CDC onboarding March–July 2027
CDC assignments begin August 2027
PHIFP orientation September 2027

The application closes at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on November 6, 2026. All applications and supporting materials must be received by the deadline, and late applications will not be accepted. Recommendation Forms have a separate deadline of November 15, 2026.

How the Selection Process Works

Following the application deadline, PHIFP screens applications for eligibility and quality.

Candidates who progress through the process may subsequently be contacted by CDC host sites for interviews. Host sites are expected to conduct interviews between January and February 2027.

Final selections are expected between February and March 2027, after which applicants will be notified of their status.

Selected candidates will then undergo CDC onboarding between March and July 2027 before beginning their assignments in August 2027. New fellows are scheduled to complete the required two-week orientation in September 2027.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should carefully assess the requirements before submitting an application.

First, applicants should confirm that their academic qualification falls within one of the eligible fields.

Second, candidates should verify that they have at least one year of documented full-time professional or volunteer experience in the same field as their qualifying degree.

Third, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate research or evaluation experience where applicable.

Fourth, candidates must be able to commit to a two-year, full-time fellowship.

Finally, applicants should carefully consider the relocation requirement because PHIFP fellows are expected to work at their assigned CDC locations and are not eligible to work remotely.

How to Prepare a Strong PHIFP Application

A strong application should make it easy for reviewers to understand the relationship between the applicant’s academic training, professional experience, research background, and interest in public health informatics.

Applicants can strengthen their preparation by:

  1. Reviewing the eligibility requirements carefully
    Confirm that the degree, field of study, professional experience, citizenship or immigration status, and other requirements are satisfied.
  2. Documenting relevant professional experience
    Clearly describe work or volunteer experience related to the applicant’s qualifying degree.
  3. Highlighting technical expertise
    Where applicable, explain experience involving data science, computer science, information systems, statistics, epidemiology, informatics, or related technologies.
  4. Demonstrating research experience
    Include relevant publications, theses, presentations, research proposals, evaluations, or comparable work.
  5. Explaining public health interests
    Show how technical expertise can be applied to public health challenges.
  6. Preparing recommendation materials early
    Since recommendation forms have a separate deadline of November 15, applicants should give recommenders sufficient time to submit their materials.
  7. Planning for relocation
    Applicants should understand that the fellowship is on-site and that relocation expenses are not covered by the program.

APPLY HERE

Deadline for the Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program

The application deadline for the CDC Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program Class of 2027 is November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

The CDC states that late applications will not be accepted, so candidates should submit their applications and supporting materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours.

Recommendation Forms are due separately by November 15, 2026.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should review the official CDC eligibility requirements and application instructions before beginning their application.

Applicants should also review the official fellowship overview and eligibility information to understand the academic, experience, citizenship, research, and relocation requirements.

Visit HERE to learn more about the CDC Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program 2027.

Conclusion

The Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program (PHIFP) Class of 2027 provides an advanced opportunity for qualified professionals to combine expertise in technology, data, informatics, and public health. Through a two-year paid fellowship, participants receive extensive practical training while contributing to CDC projects involving public health information systems, data, research, technical assistance, informatics evaluation, and emergency response.

The program’s emphasis on approximately 90% on-the-job training and 10% coursework makes it particularly relevant for professionals seeking substantial hands-on experience rather than a purely academic program. Fellows also have the opportunity to complete a capstone project and work on projects that support public health organizations.

With applications for the Class of 2027 closing on November 6, 2026, eligible professionals should begin preparing their applications early. Candidates should pay particular attention to the academic and experience requirements, research background, immigration or citizenship eligibility, two-year full-time commitment, and requirement to relocate to their assigned CDC site.

For professionals seeking to build a career where data, technology, information systems, and public health intersect, PHIFP offers a structured pathway to develop advanced skills while contributing to important public health work.

For more global fellowship opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
Are you a young person passionate about youth participation, democratic life, and creating meaningful opportunities for young people to have their voices heard? The Youth Participation Strategy (YPS) Steering Group is inviting young people aged 18 to 30 to apply for the 2026–2027 mandate.

The SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre (SALTO PI) is looking for six youth representatives with experience in the Erasmus+ and/or European Solidarity Corps programmes and a demonstrated interest in youth participation at local, national, and/or international level.

Selected youth representatives will have the opportunity to contribute directly to the work of the Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group, including monitoring and evaluating the implementation of the YPS and supporting efforts to strengthen meaningful youth participation in democratic life.

The application deadline is 9 October 2026.

What Is the Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group?

The Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group is connected to the implementation of the Youth Participation Strategy (YPS) within the framework of the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes.

The strategy focuses on strengthening meaningful youth participation in democratic life. The Steering Group brings together youth representatives and key stakeholders involved in youth participation and the implementation of the strategy.

For the 2026–2027 mandate, six young people will be selected through an open call to join representatives of important Youth Participation Strategy stakeholders and partners.

These include representatives from:

  • The European Commission
  • National Agencies
  • SALTO Resource Centres
  • The RAY Network
  • European youth umbrella organisations
  • Other key Youth Participation Strategy stakeholders and partners

This structure provides young representatives with an opportunity to work alongside organisations and institutions involved in shaping and implementing youth participation initiatives.

Call for Six Youth Representatives

SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre is seeking six youth representatives for the 2026–2027 Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group mandate.

The call is specifically aimed at young people who already have experience with Erasmus+ and/or the European Solidarity Corps and who are interested in strengthening youth participation in democratic life.

This is therefore an opportunity for young people who have moved beyond simply participating in youth programmes and have developed an understanding of youth participation, democratic engagement, or related activities.

What Will Selected Youth Representatives Do?

Becoming a member of the Steering Group involves contributing to the broader implementation and development of the Youth Participation Strategy.

According to the call, youth representatives will contribute to several important areas.

1. Support Monitoring and Evaluation of the Youth Participation Strategy

One of the responsibilities of the Steering Group is to support the full-term monitoring and evaluation of how the Youth Participation Strategy has been implemented during the 2021–2027 period.

This means representatives can contribute youth perspectives to discussions about how the strategy has been implemented and how its objectives and priorities are being addressed.

The participation of young representatives is particularly relevant because the strategy itself is focused on meaningful youth participation.

2. Promote Meaningful Youth Participation in Democratic Life

Another important responsibility is promoting the implementation of meaningful participation in democratic life.

Youth representatives will contribute to efforts to make youth participation an important priority within the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes.

The opportunity therefore connects youth participation with broader democratic engagement and encourages young people to play an active role in shaping the programmes that affect them.

3. Provide Advice on the Implementation of the Strategy

Members of the Steering Group will also have the opportunity to advise on the implementation of the Youth Participation Strategy.

This includes providing perspectives and input concerning the strategy’s priority areas.

The youth representatives can therefore contribute not only as participants but also as advisers whose experiences and perspectives can inform discussions about youth participation.

4. Contribute to Initiatives Supporting the Strategy’s Goals

The selected representatives will also have the opportunity to develop initiatives that contribute to the goals of the Youth Participation Strategy.

This provides space for representatives to move from discussion and advice toward practical contributions that support the strategy’s objectives.

Who Is SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre?

The call is organised by the SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre (SALTO PI).

SALTO PI is involved in supporting youth participation and information-related work within the broader European youth programme environment.

For this particular call, SALTO PI is looking for young people who can bring practical experience and youth perspectives into the Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group.

Eligibility Requirements

The call identifies three key areas of experience and interest that applicants should have.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be:

18 to 30 years old.

This age requirement is specifically stated in the call for youth representatives.

Experience With Erasmus+ and/or European Solidarity Corps

Applicants should have experience with the:

  • Erasmus+ programme, and/or
  • European Solidarity Corps programme

Experience with one or both of these programmes is therefore an important part of the eligibility profile.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate how their previous involvement has given them an understanding of European youth programmes and participation.

Experience in Youth Participation

Applicants should also have experience in youth participation.

This experience can be at:

  • Local level
  • National level
  • International level

The call does not limit applicants to one particular level of youth participation. Instead, experience at any of these levels can be relevant.

Interest in Strengthening Youth Participation

Applicants should have a genuine interest in strengthening youth participation in the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes.

This means that applicants should be able to demonstrate an interest in improving how young people participate in democratic life and how youth participation can be meaningfully incorporated into these programmes.

Key Eligibility Criteria at a Glance

Applicants should meet the following profile:

  1. Be 18–30 years old.
  2. Have experience with Erasmus+ and/or the European Solidarity Corps.
  3. Have experience in youth participation at local, national, and/or international level.
  4. Have an interest in strengthening youth participation within the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes.

Why This Opportunity Matters for Young People

Youth participation is not only about allowing young people to express their opinions. Meaningful participation involves creating opportunities for young people to contribute to decisions, initiatives, and processes that affect their lives and communities.

The YPS Steering Group provides a structure through which young representatives can contribute their experiences to discussions about youth participation at a broader European programme level.

For selected participants, this can provide exposure to the work of major stakeholders involved in youth participation, including European institutions, National Agencies, SALTO Resource Centres, youth organisations, and research networks.

Opportunity to Work With Key European Youth Stakeholders

The Steering Group will not consist exclusively of the six youth representatives.

It will also include representatives from key Youth Participation Strategy stakeholders and partners.

These include:

  • European Commission representatives
  • National Agencies
  • SALTO Resource Centres
  • RAY Network representatives
  • European youth umbrella organisations

This creates a collaborative environment where young representatives can contribute alongside organisations and institutions with responsibilities related to youth participation.

What Kind of Applicant Is the Call Looking For?

The call is particularly suited to young people who can combine practical experience, youth participation knowledge, and an interest in democratic engagement.

A strong applicant would ideally be able to demonstrate:

  • Previous participation in Erasmus+ and/or European Solidarity Corps activities
  • Practical involvement in youth participation
  • Experience working with or for young people
  • Experience at local, national, or international level
  • Interest in democratic participation
  • Understanding of the importance of meaningful youth involvement
  • Motivation to strengthen participation within European youth programmes

The provided call does not state that applicants need a particular university degree or specific academic qualification.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group 2026–2027 is:

9 October 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline through the designated online application form.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted online through the official application form provided in the call.

Application Form:

Apply to Become a Youth Representative

Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the role description before completing their application so they understand the expectations associated with membership of the Steering Group.

Further Information About the Role

The full role description is available through the application materials provided with the call.

The call also provides a link to information about the work of the previous Steering Group, allowing prospective applicants to gain a better understanding of how co-steering has contributed to Europe’s youth participation strategy.

Read About the Previous Steering Group’s Work. 

learn more hERE

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because only six youth representatives will be selected, applicants should make their application as relevant and convincing as possible.

1. Demonstrate Your Erasmus+ or European Solidarity Corps Experience

Clearly explain your experience with Erasmus+ and/or the European Solidarity Corps.

Rather than simply listing activities, explain what you learned and how the experience contributed to your understanding of youth participation.

2. Highlight Your Youth Participation Experience

Describe the youth participation activities you have been involved in.

This could include experience at:

  • Local level
  • National level
  • International level

Make clear what your role was and how you contributed.

3. Explain Why Youth Participation Matters to You

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine interest in strengthening youth participation.

Explain what meaningful youth participation means from your perspective and why you believe young people should have a stronger role in democratic life.

4. Connect Your Experience to Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps

The opportunity specifically focuses on strengthening youth participation within these programmes.

Applicants should therefore explain how their experience could help contribute to this objective.

5. Think Beyond Personal Benefits

A strong application should demonstrate not only what the applicant hopes to gain but also what they can contribute.

Consider explaining:

  • What perspective you would bring as a young representative
  • What you have learned from your youth participation experience
  • What challenges young people face when trying to participate
  • How participation could be made more meaningful
  • What you could contribute to the Steering Group’s discussions and initiatives

Questions and Technical Support

saltoparticipation@harno.ee

This contact is specifically provided for questions or technical issues related to the application process.

Conclusion

The Youth Participation Strategy Steering Group 2026–2027 offers young people an opportunity to take an active role in shaping and strengthening youth participation within the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps programmes.

SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre is seeking six young representatives aged 18 to 30 who have experience with Erasmus+ and/or the European Solidarity Corps, experience in youth participation at local, national and/or international level, and a strong interest in strengthening young people’s participation in democratic life.

Selected representatives will contribute to the monitoring and evaluation of the Youth Participation Strategy for the 2021–2027 period, advise on its implementation and priority areas, promote meaningful participation, and contribute to initiatives supporting the strategy’s goals.

With the Steering Group bringing together young representatives and key stakeholders such as the European Commission, National Agencies, SALTO Resource Centres, the RAY Network, and European youth umbrella organisations, the opportunity provides a platform for young people to contribute their experiences and perspectives to European youth participation work.

item.content:encoded:
International Justice Mission (IJM) offers internship and fellowship opportunities for people who want to use their skills, professional experience, and passion for justice to contribute to the mission of building a safer and more just world. These opportunities provide participants with the chance to gain practical experience, receive mentorship, and serve communities through IJM’s work.

The opportunities are available in both D.C.-based and remote settings as well as through global internships and fellowships, creating different pathways for university students, law graduates, bachelor’s degree holders, and experienced professionals to become involved in IJM’s mission.

About the IJM Internship and Fellowship Opportunities

International Justice Mission is seeking individuals who want to combine their professional abilities with a commitment to justice and community service. The organization encourages applicants to bring their passion, skills, and experiences and use them in service around the world.

The internship and fellowship opportunities are designed around the idea that different professional backgrounds and skill sets can contribute to the organization’s broader mission.

Whether someone is still developing their professional experience as a university student, has completed a Juris Doctor degree, holds a bachelor’s degree, or is an experienced professional, IJM provides several opportunities to explore how their skills can contribute to justice-focused work.

Why Consider an IJM Internship or Fellowship?

An IJM internship or fellowship can provide more than professional experience. The organization highlights both spiritual mentorship and professional mentorship as important parts of the experience.

Participants can expect opportunities to develop personally and professionally while working within an organization focused on justice.

1. Spiritual Mentorship

IJM describes spiritual mentorship as an important part of its internship and fellowship experience.

Participants have the opportunity to grow spiritually within an organization that practices spiritual formation together on a daily basis. This provides an environment in which participants can explore personal growth alongside their professional responsibilities.

2. Professional Mentorship

Professional mentorship is another key component of the program.

Interns and fellows can develop professional skills while receiving career mentorship from individuals who are invested in helping them grow and succeed.

This mentorship can be valuable for participants who want to understand how their academic background, professional skills, and personal interests can be applied in a justice-oriented organization.

D.C.-Based and Remote Internships and Fellowships

One of the main pathways offered by IJM is its D.C.-based and remote internships and fellowships.

These opportunities are particularly relevant for university students and legal professionals who are interested in gaining experience without necessarily undertaking a global deployment.

Duration

The D.C.-based and remote opportunities generally include:

  • 2–3 month internships and fellowships for second-year university students and beyond.
  • 6–12 month legal fellowship opportunities for individuals who have earned a Juris Doctor degree.

This structure means that applicants can identify opportunities according to their current stage of education and professional development.

Who Can Benefit From These Opportunities?

The short-term internships and fellowships are designed for second-year university students and students beyond their second year.

For applicants pursuing legal careers, IJM also provides a longer legal fellowship pathway for individuals who have completed a Juris Doctor degree.

Applicants should review the individual position descriptions on the IJM careers platform because specific requirements can vary depending on the position.

D.C. and Remote Application Periods

IJM provides different application periods depending on when participants want to serve.

Spring Opportunities

Spring service generally takes place from:

January – April

Applications for spring opportunities open in:

June

Summer Opportunities

Summer service generally takes place from:

May – August

Applications for summer opportunities open in:

October

Fall Opportunities

Fall service generally takes place from:

September – December

Applications for fall opportunities open in:

March

Because applications open several months before the relevant service period, prospective applicants should begin preparing well in advance.

Global Internships and Fellowships

IJM also provides global internships and fellowships for individuals who want to serve internationally.

These opportunities are structured differently from the D.C.-based and remote options and are intended for applicants with a bachelor’s degree and/or significant professional experience.

Duration of Global Opportunities

Global internships and fellowships are generally 12-month opportunities.

They are available for:

  • Individuals with a bachelor’s degree
  • Seasoned professionals
  • Applicants who have relevant skills and experience that can contribute to IJM’s work

These opportunities can provide an opportunity to work in an international setting while contributing professional expertise to IJM’s mission.

Global Deployment Schedule

Global deployments occur annually, with deployments scheduled for:

  • January
  • June

Because these are international opportunities, applicants should plan well in advance.

IJM states that applications generally open 11–12 months before the deployment date.

This means prospective applicants should not wait until shortly before the intended deployment period to begin looking for opportunities.

For example, someone interested in a January deployment should begin monitoring available positions approximately 11–12 months beforehand, while someone interested in a June deployment should similarly begin preparing well in advance.

What Skills Can You Bring to IJM?

IJM emphasizes that applicants should bring their passion, skills, and experiences to the organization.

The opportunity is therefore not limited to one particular academic discipline or professional background in the information provided.

Instead, IJM highlights the importance of different skill sets in contributing to its mission.

Applicants should review the current vacancies carefully and identify positions that match their:

  • Educational background
  • Professional experience
  • Technical skills
  • Career interests
  • Personal strengths
  • Commitment to justice and service

The exact qualifications will depend on the specific internship or fellowship position.

How to Apply for an IJM Internship or Fellowship

Applicants interested in these opportunities should begin by reviewing IJM’s current available positions.

The organization specifically instructs prospective applicants to click “Apply Now” to view current positions.

Application Portal:

Apply Now – IJM Careers

Because positions and requirements may change, applicants should review the individual vacancy carefully before submitting an application.

Application Timeline at a Glance

Opportunity Duration Intended Applicants Service Period Application Timing
D.C.-based/Remote Internship 2–3 months Second-year university students and beyond Spring, Summer, Fall Opens several months before service
D.C.-based/Remote Fellowship 2–3 months Eligible students and applicants depending on position Spring, Summer, Fall Opens several months before service
Legal Fellowship 6–12 months Juris Doctor graduates Based on available position Check current vacancies
Global Internship/Fellowship 12 months Bachelor’s degree holders and/or seasoned professionals January and June deployments Opens 11–12 months before deployment

Important Deadlines and Application Dates

There is no single universal application deadline stated for all IJM internships and fellowships. Instead, application timing depends on the specific opportunity and service period.

For D.C.-based and remote opportunities:

  • Spring (January–April): Applications open in June
  • Summer (May–August): Applications open in October
  • Fall (September–December): Applications open in March

For global opportunities:

  • Deployments take place in January and June each year.
  • Applications generally open 11–12 months before the deployment date.

Applicants should therefore check the current IJM careers page for the exact opening and closing dates associated with the position they are interested in.

How to Prepare for an IJM Application

Since IJM offers different internships and fellowships, preparation should be tailored to the specific position.

1. Identify the Right Opportunity

Start by reviewing the current positions available through IJM’s careers platform.

Look for opportunities that correspond to your education, professional experience, skills, and career objectives.

2. Review the Position Requirements

Do not assume that all IJM internships and fellowships have identical eligibility requirements.

Carefully read the description of the specific position to determine:

  • Required educational qualifications
  • Required professional experience
  • Specific skills
  • Location
  • Duration
  • Service period
  • Any position-specific requirements

3. Prepare to Explain Your Motivation

IJM’s opportunities are connected to its broader mission of building a safer and more just world.

Applicants should be prepared to clearly communicate why they are interested in justice-focused work and how their skills and experiences could contribute to the organization.

4. Highlight Relevant Skills and Experience

Your application should clearly demonstrate the strengths you would bring to the organization.

Depending on the position, relevant experience could include academic projects, professional work, legal experience, research, communications, administration, technology, advocacy, or other skills required by the specific role.

5. Apply Early

For global fellowships and internships in particular, early preparation is important because applications open 11–12 months before deployment.

Planning ahead gives applicants more time to identify an appropriate position and prepare a strong application.

APPLY here

An Opportunity to Combine Professional Growth With Service

What distinguishes these opportunities is the combination of career development, mentorship, and service.

Rather than viewing an internship or fellowship simply as a temporary professional placement, IJM presents these opportunities as a way for participants to contribute their abilities toward a broader mission.

The combination of spiritual and professional mentorship can also give participants an opportunity to develop in multiple areas during their time with the organization.

For university students, the experience can help connect academic learning with practical work. For legal professionals, the legal fellowship provides a longer-term opportunity to apply legal training. For bachelor’s degree holders and experienced professionals, global opportunities provide a pathway to contribute skills in an international context.

Learn more HERE

Conclusion

The International Justice Mission (IJM) Internship and Fellowship Opportunities provide multiple pathways for students, legal professionals, graduates, and experienced professionals who want to combine professional development with meaningful service.

With D.C.-based and remote internships and fellowships, legal fellowship opportunities, and 12-month global internships and fellowships, applicants can explore opportunities that correspond to different stages of their education and careers.

Participants can benefit from both spiritual mentorship and professional mentorship, while gaining experience within an organization committed to building a safer and more just world.

There is no single deadline for all positions. D.C.-based and remote opportunities follow seasonal application periods, while global opportunities generally open applications 11–12 months before January or June deployments. Prospective applicants should therefore monitor the IJM careers portal and apply for positions that match their qualifications and interests.
